findings.headline: Remove ref from this Portal; Solid 2's Portal takes only mount and children.
findings.why: Solid 1.x passed the Portal's wrapper <div> to ref. Solid 2.0.3's Portal has no wrapper element and no ref prop: it inserts its children directly into mount.
findings.guidance: Put the ref on an element you render inside the Portal (wrap the children in your own <div ref={...}> if code needs one element), or pass mount an element you hold a ref to.

findings.headline: Remove useShadow from this Portal; Solid 2's Portal takes only mount and children.
findings.why: Solid 2.0.3's Portal has no useShadow option; it inserts its children directly into mount and attaches no shadow root.
findings.guidance: Create the shadow root yourself (host.attachShadow({ mode: "open" })) and pass it, or an element inside it, as mount.

findings.headline: Remove isSVG from this Portal; Solid 2's Portal takes only mount and children.
findings.why: Solid 2.0.3's Portal has no isSVG option; it inserts its children directly into mount, so SVG content goes into an SVG mount as is.
findings.guidance: Pass an SVG element as mount and render SVG children; there is no wrapper <g> to opt into.

findings.headline: Check code and CSS that find this Portal's content through its wrapper <div>.
findings.why: Solid 1.x rendered a Portal's children inside a <div> it appended to mount. Solid 2.0.3's Portal (still imported from @solidjs/web) inserts the children directly into mount between empty text nodes, and renders nothing on the server, so mount.firstChild, #root > div selectors and styles on that div no longer match.
findings.guidance: If anything relied on the wrapper, render your own element inside the Portal and target it. Async reads inside a Portal start on the client; give them their own <Loading> boundary.
